settings.title:
Identify AI Security Risks Before
They Become Business Risks
AI Introduces Security Risks Across the Entire AI Environment

settings.editor: AI security isn't limited to the model itself.

An AI application may connect to business data, external APIs, internal systems, users, applications, and third-party platforms. Each connection can introduce another point where security controls need to be evaluated.
Without a clear assessment, it can be difficult to know:
01Where sensitive data enters or leaves AI workflows
02Which users, applications, or systems can access AI resources
03Whether integrations introduce unnecessary exposure
04Whether AI applications have appropriate security controls
05Which risks require immediate attention

settings.title: What Is an AI Security Assessment?

settings.editor: A Security Review Built Around How Your AI Actually Works

settings.css_classes: f3-aia-stack f3-aia-stack--20 f3-aia-col-664 f3-rv f3m-a32414e f3g-fd51394

settings.editor: An AI Security Assessment evaluates the security of your AI applications, platforms, integrations, data flows, access controls, and supporting environment to identify weaknesses and security risks.
Rather than assessing AI as a standalone technology, the assessment looks at how AI interacts with users, data, applications, systems, and integrations.
The goal is straightforward:
Understand the risks. Prioritize what matters. Know what to address next.

settings.title: Why Does Your AI Environment Need a Security Assessment?

settings.css_classes: f3-aia-stack f3-aia-stack--20 f3-aia-why__aside f3-rv f3m-3955da7 f3g-ecbaaec

settings.editor: AI adoption can move quickly. Security reviews need to keep pace.
AI applications may interact with confidential business information, customer data, intellectual property, and other sensitive content.

settings.title: AI Expands the Application Attack Surface

settings.editor: AI applications introduce additional components, integrations, APIs, prompts, workflows, and interactions that may require security review.

settings.title: Access Can Extend Across Multiple Systems

settings.editor: AI applications and platforms may interact with users, applications, services, and business systems, making access controls an important part of the security assessment.

settings.title: Existing Security Reviews May Not Cover AI-Specific Risks

settings.editor: Traditional application, infrastructure, or cloud assessments may not evaluate how AI-specific components behave or interact.

settings.title: AI Security Risks Are Difficult to See in Isolation

settings.editor: A configuration may appear secure individually while creating risk when connected to another application, integration, data source, or user.

settings.title: Build Security Into Your AI Journey

settings.editor: Assessing AI environments early can help security and technology teams understand risks before AI becomes deeply embedded into business workflows.
Identify security considerations before an AI application or platform enters production.
Review how AI connects with applications, APIs, data, and users.
Reassess security as new AI applications, platforms, integrations, and workflows are introduced.
Keep security considerations aligned with changes to applications, data, access, and AI architecture.

items.item_title: How is a Virtual CIO different from Managed IT Services?
Is a Virtual CIO right for small and mid-sized businesses?
Can a Virtual CIO help with cybersecurity and compliance?
Ready to Build a Smarter Technology Strategy?

settings.editor: Yes. Many growing businesses need executive technology guidance but don't require a full-time CIO. A Virtual CIO provides access to senior technology expertise on a flexible basis, making it easier to plan for growth, manage risk, and align IT with business objectives.
Know Where Your AI Security Risks Begin
AI can create new connections between applications, data, users, platforms, and business systems. Before those connections become difficult to secure, understand how your AI environment is exposed.
